• The GSAT-20 is a Ka-band high throughput communication satellite launched by NSIL.
 
• GSAT-20 aims to provide broadband connectivity in the Ka-band over the Indian region, supporting Digital India initiatives.
 
• NSIL's role includes satellite building, launching, and providing space-based services on demand.

• **Ka-band Frequency**

 
 
• The Ka-band refers to the frequency range from 26.5 to 40 GHz, used primarily for satellite communications.
 
• It offers higher bandwidth compared to other bands, enabling faster data transmission rates.
 
 
 
• **High Throughput Satellites (HTS)**
 
 
• HTS are advanced satellites that provide more bandwidth and higher data rates compared to traditional satellites.
 
• They use multiple spot beams to increase capacity and improve coverage, especially in underserved regions.
 
 
 
• **Digital India Initiative**
 
 
• An initiative by the Government of India aimed at ensuring the availability of government services electronically, improving online infrastructure, and increasing internet connectivity.
 
• It aims to empower citizens with digital literacy and bridge the digital divide.
 
 
 
• **Department of Space (DoS)**
 
 
• DoS is responsible for the development of space technology and the application of satellite communications and meteorology in India.
 
• It oversees organizations like ISRO and NSIL.

questions.question: The PARAM Rudra supercomputer was inaugurated at which institute on 27 September 2024?

options.text: S.N. Bose National Centre for Basic Sciences (SNBNCBS), Kolkata

questions.question: In September 2024, researchers at (the) _______ developed a 'brain on a chip' that can store and process data in 16,500 states within molecular film.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian Institute of Science (IISc)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In September 2024, researchers at the **Indian Institute of Science (IISc)** developed a 'brain on a chip' technology.
 
• The 'brain on a chip' can store and process data in **16,500 states within a molecular film**.
 
• This innovation is significant in the field of **neuromorphic engineering**, which aims to mimic the neural architecture of the human brain.
 
• The development represents a major advancement in **data processing capabilities** and storage efficiency.
 
• The research was conducted by a team of scientists from the **Centre for Nano Science and Engineering (CeNSE) at IISc**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Neuromorphic Engineering**

 
 
• A field of engineering focused on creating artificial systems that mimic the neural architecture of the human brain.
 
• It combines principles from neuroscience, biology, physics, computer science, and electrical engineering.
 
• The goal is to develop hardware that can perform complex tasks efficiently, similar to the human brain.
 
 
 
• **Molecular Electronics**
 
 
• Involves using molecules as the fundamental building blocks for electronic devices.
 
• It aims to develop components that can perform electronic functions at a molecular level.
 
• Molecular electronics is key to advancements in miniaturization and efficiency of devices.
 
 
 
• **Data Storage Technologies**
 
 
• Methods and devices used to store digital data, ranging from traditional hard drives to advanced molecular storage.
 
• Advances in storage technologies aim to increase capacity, speed, and reliability.
 
• Emerging technologies include DNA data storage, quantum storage, and neuromorphic storage devices.
 
 
 
• **Centre for Nano Science and Engineering (CeNSE)**
 
 
• Part of the Indian Institute of Science (IISc) in Bangalore, India.
 
• Focuses on research and development in the field of nanotechnology.
 
• CeNSE aims to foster innovation in nano science and engineering with applications in various fields such as electronics, materials science, and biotechnology.
